thread:
sam: Heads up — saw a 6-8% p99 CPU bump on host side in last canary, looks tied to yesterday's kernel-selector + grpc writer change.

anika: Saw that too. Quick flame shows an extra memcpy in host_tokenizer::splice_buffer introduced by the stream refactor. @prashant any ideas?

prashant: I pushed the chunk-aligned write to reduce HTTP2 fragments, but it looks like small chunks now follow a copy path when chunk_size < MIN_SPLICE. Stack simplified: 
```
# simplified stack
host_tokenizer::splice_buffer
-> grpc_stream::write_chunk (copy path)
-> http2_out::frame_queue
```

lee: Do we have perf traces or a flamegraph?

perf-bot: perf report: host_tokenize_splice 32% CPU, grpc_write_chunk_copy 18%, malloc/free ~9% (attached in artifact).

anika: Repro on a 64-token seq workload: batching heuristic emits ~16 tokens/chunk, lots of tiny writes, malloc/free thrash. Snippet: 
```
requests: seq=60 tokens=12 chunks=5
writes: 12x 256B allocs
```

prashant: Options: 1) add a fast-path zero-copy for chunk <= 16 tokens, 2) increase coalesce_window in grpc writer to absorb small writes, 3) revert the refactor and rethink.

sam: Can we try 1+2 first? I can spin a canary with a small patch. :thumbsup:

lee: Also check KV cache locality — more tiny chunks might reduce kvcache hit locality and cause extra RPCs.

anika: Good call. Instrumented kvcache hit-rate by request chunk size — small-chunk requests drop hit rate ~4% and increase lookups by ~6% (sample).

prashant: Uploading a wip PR with zero-copy path + coalesce_window bump to 48ms on canary branch: <https://git/repo/pull/1234>. Includes unit test and perf harness.

sam: Nice. Run canary in low-traffic window tonight, monitor p99, cpu_delta, kvcache_hit. If green, roll forward with staged ramp. :rocket:
